topic: PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: At one fixed smooth boundary point b, observe iid units from a uniform two-sided half-disc with Bernoulli outcomes whose side means lie in [1/4,3/4] and are L-Lipschitz, but retain only treatment side and radial point-distance Q_Delta(R)=Delta floor(R/Delta), not angle or raw coordinates. Target tau(b). Prove minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order max{n^(-1/4),Delta}, with squared risk of the corresponding squared order, uniformly across Delta, using a bin-aware local estimator with explicit Lipschitz bias. The lower seed is exact: on the treated first bin set phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u), u=R/Delta; half-disc radial density is proportional to u and integral_0^1 u phi(u)du=0, so a Bernoulli-mean perturbation c Delta phi gives the same rounded-bin law while changing the boundary limit by c Delta and retaining bounded derivative. The rd2d.distance R, Python, and Stata workflow and its Ser Pilo Paga replication are the consumer. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a same-class lower combining sampling and aliasing rather than merely maximizing separate bounds, construct total honest intervals for all Delta regimes, and state exactly what coordinate coarsening the analyst observes. EARLY KILL TEST: Drop if Dong-Kolesar or discrete-running-variable RD already yields this 2D radial-compression point-BATEC frontier, if the weighted integral identity or Bernoulli-mixture equality fails, or if raw coordinates remain available.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the uniform joint sampling-and-aliasing minimax frontier for a fixed-point boundary treatment effect when the analyst observes only treatment side and floor-rounded point-radius.

source_refs.claim: For exact scalar distances in boundary-discontinuity designs, the paper derives the radial n^(-1/4) minimax limitation but does not analyze rounded distances.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocío Titiunik, and Ruiqi Rae Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu supply the exact-distance radial sampling problem, while Dong and Kolesár–Rothe treat rounding or discrete support for an ordinary one-score RD. The rejected heaping proposal gives a reusable within-cell null direction, and the accepted boundary-distance proposal gives a radial sampling converse, but neither verifies their coexistence in the present Bernoulli/Lipschitz half-disc experiment. The concrete missing step is a regime-indexed least-favorable construction that preserves the Bernoulli range and derivative bound, uses the u-weighted first-bin null direction for the Δ component, uses an h²-local-mass bump for the n^(-1/4) component, and controls testing distance uniformly at the transition Δ comparable to n^(-1/4). Targeted searches found no paper treating the observation operator (side, floor(R/Δ)) at a fixed two-dimensional boundary point.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem with constants c and C, uniform over 0 < Δ ≤ Δ0, that sandwiches minimax absolute risk between c max{n^(-1/4), Δ} and C max{n^(-1/4), Δ}, gives the corresponding squared-risk bounds, and supplies legal same-class testing alternatives plus a matching bin-aware estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing treats scalar-distance boundary inference as a deliberate information reduction and links the rate theory to rd2d and Ser Pilo Paga.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Boundary designs begin with bivariate scores -> practitioners compress location to scalar point-distance -> radial localization has an n^(-1/4) information limit -> releasing only rounded radius may add an exact aliasing floor.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over distance-based local-polynomial bias and variance analysis with effective local mass h², together with the pointwise radial minimax testing argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact-distance experiment has the same half-disc radial mass scaling; the first change is replacing exact-radius kernel moments and likelihoods by rounded-bin moments.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent rounding as integration over latent running-variable cells and analyze the resulting discretization bias or identified bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired alias is a null direction of a rounding-cell integral, modified here by the radial Jacobian proportional to r.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute a modulus of continuity over a convex smoothness class and derive minimax estimators and confidence procedures from the same modulus.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The rounded radial model is a linear-functional problem over a convex Lipschitz class with a bin-averaging observation operator.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a total honest confidence interval for the fixed-point boundary treatment effect that remains defined with empty or sparse radial bins and attains expected length of order max{n^(-1/4), Δ} in every quantization regime.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives pointwise and uniform inference for exact distances under regularity and effective-sample-size conditions, not total inference with rounded sparse bins.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocío Titiunik, and Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: Worst-case smoothness bias and bias-aware critical values yield honest, near-optimal intervals for nonparametric regression and ordinary RD.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

open_problems.why_unsolved: The exact-distance boundary theory requires enough local observations, while rounded radial data can leave the first useful bins empty or make their Gram statistic singular when Δ is comparable to or larger than n^(-1/4). Ordinary discrete-RD intervals do not incorporate radial bin probabilities of order Δ² or the latent within-bin Lipschitz bias. The prior thickness run also leaves sharp pointwise honest width unresolved. The first proof step that changes is replacing full-distance local calibration by grouped Bernoulli cell statistics and an explicit within-bin bias envelope, including a fallback confidence set on sparse-count events without losing the optimal expected-length transition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified confidence set C(n,Δ), including its sparse-bin fallback rule, with uniform coverage at least 1-α over the Bernoulli/Lipschitz half-disc class and supremum expected length bounded above and below by constants times max{n^(-1/4), Δ}.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from a common invalid inference practice to explicit misspecification bias and then to guaranteed-coverage alternatives.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Coarse support invalidates conventional standard-error logic -> smoothness restrictions quantify hidden bias -> honest intervals replace clustered inference -> radial binning additionally demands geometry-aware bias and totality under sparse random counts.

method_exemplars.technique: Add an explicit worst-case bias bound to the standard-error term and optimize weights or bandwidth for honest expected length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A bin-aware Lipschitz estimator has a deterministic bias envelope, but its proof must also cover random bin degeneracy.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct guaranteed-coverage intervals on discrete support by bounding specification error instead of treating support points as clusters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rounded radii create discrete support whose probabilities vanish quadratically near the target.

method_exemplars.technique: Use studentized distance-based local-polynomial inference with the correct n h² variance normalization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the boundary-design variance and side decomposition that a rounded-bin interval must retain.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the fixed-point minimax information ordering across full raw coordinates, exact point-radius, side plus rounded point-radius, rounded Cartesian coordinates, and point-radius plus angle, identifying exactly which retained coordinates eliminate the Δ aliasing term.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The geographic and boundary-discontinuity papers establish that information loss depends on which spatial coordinates are discarded, but their comparisons use exact distance and often target an entire boundary or irregular geometry. At one fixed smooth point, point-radius localizes b even without angle, so their negative results cannot simply be imported; floor quantization instead creates a within-annulus equivalence. A reviewer of the prior boundary-distance proposal explicitly requested a distance-only versus full-location benchmark. The missing proof is an experiment-level likelihood factorization for each observation sigma-field, with indistinguishable alternatives showing whether angle, within-bin position, or raw coordinates break the Δ alias.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem or deficiency/minimax comparison table assigning every stated observation sigma-field a sharp absolute- and squared-risk rate, with explicit equivalence pairs and necessary-and-sufficient retained information for eliminating the order-Δ term.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes the observation choice substantive and explains geometrically why scalar distance can fail to encode the target location.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A geographic boundary is intrinsically two-dimensional -> scalar distance merges locations -> merged locations may carry different boundary effects -> fixed-point theory must state exactly which coordinates survive coarsening.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare scalar-distance and full-coordinate procedures through matched local-polynomial upper bounds and separate minimax lower experiments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result refines this information comparison by inserting deterministic radial quantization at a fixed smooth boundary point.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bivariate-score local-polynomial estimation and pointwise boundary inference as the full-coordinate benchmark.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the procedure and limit theory against which rounded-radius and radius-plus-angle experiments should be compared.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize finite-sample minimax linear weights under smoothness constraints for discrete, continuous, and multiple-running-variable RD designs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same optimization exposes how feasible bias-variance tradeoffs change as the observed coordinate sigma-field expands.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the rounded-radial frontier remains max{n^(-1/4), Δ} for a curved smooth boundary with an unknown nonuniform local design density, and characterize the local radial-weight conditions that permit an order-Δ within-bin alias.

source_refs.claim: Exact-distance boundary inference allows general continuous bivariate design densities and shows that local geometry controls bias and feasible rates.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocío Titiunik, and Ruiqi Rae Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The uniform half-disc makes the first-bin weight exactly proportional to u, so the displayed polynomial has zero weighted mean and preserves the rounded Bernoulli mixture. Curvature and an unknown density replace that weight by a side-specific tubular-coordinate Jacobian and latent radial density. Exact-distance boundary theory can expand these quantities when locations are observed, and one-score rounding theory can posit or estimate a rounding law, but neither shows that an implementable density-free grouped estimator and a weighted alias survive when raw locations are unavailable. The first changed proof step is therefore a weighted moment-zero construction with uniform derivative and Bernoulli-range control, followed by grouped-count upper bounds that do not assume unobservable local Gram coercivity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient local radial-weight condition and explicit weighted-orthogonal Lipschitz perturbation, together with a total bin estimator, matching minimax risk, and honest-length bounds over a declared class of curved boundaries and smooth nonuniform densities.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central narrative makes geometry and design density determinants of the interpretation, bias, and variance of distance-based boundary inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Distance methods handle general treatment boundaries -> geometry and density determine the induced radial law -> rounding aliases depend on that latent radial weight -> characterize exactly when the half-disc frontier transfers.

method_exemplars.technique: Use coarea or tubular-coordinate radial expansions, distance-local polynomial estimation, and explicit geometric smoothing-bias control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first proof change replaces exact-distance integrals by sums over quantized annuli carrying the same local Jacobian.

method_exemplars.technique: Integrate latent running-variable values over rounding cells and separate correction under a known cell law from bounds under an unknown law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Unknown within-annulus density plays the role of an unknown rounding distribution, with cell weights inherited from two-dimensional geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Use empirical local design mass and Lepski comparison to select a pointwise bandwidth under an inhomogeneous random design.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Grouped counts are the remaining observable signal for calibrating effective radial information when the density is unknown.

literature_map:
Keele and Titiunik (2015, Political Analysis, doi:10.1093/pan/mpu014) establish geographic RD and show why scalar boundary distance generally does not isolate a particular boundary location.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2025, arXiv:2505.05670) develop location-based pointwise and uniform inference using the full bivariate score and document failures of distance reduction at irregular boundaries.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2026.106266; arXiv:2510.26051) develop exact-distance BATEC inference and the radial n^(-1/4) minimax limitation.
That 2026 paper's Ser Pilo Paga application uses raw bivariate scores and computed exact distances; it does not study released data containing only rounded point-radius.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2025, arXiv:2505.07989) document rd2d's bivariate and exact-distance workflows; the scan found no quantization-aware rd2d estimator.
Kolesár and Rothe (2018, AER, doi:10.1257/aer.20160945; arXiv:1606.04086) show that clustering by discrete support values does not repair misspecification bias and propose honest smoothness-based alternatives.
Dong (2015, JAE, doi:10.1002/jae.2369) proves inconsistency from one-dimensional rounding, gives corrections using the rounding-error law, and supplies bounds when that law is unknown.
Dong and Kolesár (2023, JAE, doi:10.1002/jae.2974; arXiv:2111.07388) show that correctly classifying measurement error can support a causal effect conditional on the observed score, generally not the latent cutoff effect.
Davezies and Le Barbanchon (2017, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2017.06.010) recover an RD LATE with continuous measurement error using auxiliary discrepancy data absent here.
Bartalotti, Brummet, and Dieterle (2021, JBES, doi:10.1080/07350015.2020.1737081) correct group-specific running-variable mismeasurement, emphasizing dependence on an explicit error mechanism.
Barreca, Lindo, and Waddell (2016, Economic Inquiry, doi:10.1111/ecin.12225) show that outcome-related heaping can bias RD and evade ordinary diagnostics, motivating an exact observation protocol.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA14434; arXiv:1511.06028) provide modulus-based optimal inference for linear functionals over convex smoothness classes.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics, doi:10.3982/QE1199; arXiv:1606.01200) give simple bias-aware honest intervals, but not total intervals for random sparse radial bins.
Imbens and Wager (2019, Review of Economics and Statistics, doi:10.1162/rest_a_00793; arXiv:1705.01677) optimize finite-sample minimax linear RD estimators and cover discrete and multiple running variables.
Gaïffas (2005, Mathematical Methods of Statistics, arXiv:math/0410354) gives pointwise minimax rates under vanishing random-design density; the targeted scan found no published floor-rounded radial-compression frontier at a fixed two-dimensional RD boundary point.
